name: fantom
why: An object-oriented language targeting multiple runtimes with an unusual design, a close call worth a second look.

brief.what_it_is: Fantom is an object-oriented programming language that the homepage describes as portable, running on the JVM and in modern web browsers. Its syntax is Java-like, with static and dynamic typing, a system library, closures, immutability, and actor concurrency. The Homebrew package installs a set of command-line tools: fan, fanc, fanlaunch, fanp, fanr, fansh, fansubstitute, fant, flux, and jstub, plus Windows .bat variants. I did not read docs that describe what each tool takes in or produces.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit problem statement. It presents Fantom as a portable language that combines a familiar Java-like syntax with features such as closures, immutability, and actor concurrency.
brief.install_notes: The homepage offers a Download Fantom button, but I could not retrieve the downloads or install documentation. The two doc URLs I guessed returned 404, so I have no first-run steps, runtime requirements, or configuration details. The Homebrew package ships .bat files alongside the Unix executables, which suggests Windows is supported.
brief.standout: Fantom targets both the JVM and browsers from one language, and its homepage pitches an Eggbox pod repository for libraries. The Hello World example is a plain Java-style class with a static main method. The scout note calls the design unusual, but I did not find evidence in the pages I read to back that up.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage has Blog, Downloads, and Forum sections, but I saw no release date, commit history, or version number, and the Downloads page I guessed returned 404.
brief.caveats: I read only the homepage. The docs and downloads pages I tried returned 404, so install steps, licensing, platform details, and feature limits are unverified. The Homebrew caveats field is empty.
quotes: Fantom is a portable language that runs on the JVM and modern web browsers.
